title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 19/27 — "The Handling-Machine"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 19. After eating, the narrator wakes in the thudding scullery to find the curate already at the triangular opening, watching the Martians through the wall. The narrator crosses the floor on his knees, each boot placed among the broken crockery, and his fingers find the curate's leg. The whole body springs, and plaster thunders down outside.

Through the fresh slit the narrator sees the roadway turned into a circular excavation. The house has burst into rubble, the fifth cylinder lies beneath the old foundations, green vapour crosses the opening, and a deserted fighting-machine watches from the far rim. A glittering workman draws rods and plates from the cylinder with three reaching tentacles.

Then he studies the Martians themselves: round bodies, immense eyes, beaks, ears and clustered hands. When he looks again the handling-machine is shaping its parts while a smaller digger traces the rim of the pit. The machine works with no visible Martian directing it, and the curate gives the episode its closing thought: "The work goes on without a master."

Chapter II of Book Two of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "What We Saw from the Ruined House", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
